712103.full: στίγμα -τος, τό (στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Sng.1:11 (נְקֻדָּה) * ;] a tattoed mark or brand: τὰ σ. τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Gal.6:17 (see Lft., in l; Deiss., BS, 349; LAE, 303; MM, xxiii).† (AS)

712104.full: στιγμή, -ῆς, ἡ (στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Isa.29:5 (פֶּתַע), 2Ma.9:11 * ;] a prick, a point; metaphorically, σ. χρόνου, a moment: Luk.4:5.† (AS)

712105.full: punctured , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;generally, spotted, dappled , (Sophocles Tragicus); στικτὰ ὄμματα, of the hundred eyes of Argus, (Euripides) (ML)

712106.full: στίλβω [in LXX: Nam.3:3 (לַהַב), etc. ;] to shine, glisten: Mrk.9:3.† (AS)

712113.full: 1. a row or file of soldiers, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. a line of poetry, a verse , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

712114.full: στοά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX: Eze.40:18 (רִצְפָּה), etc. ;] a portico: Jhn.5:2; used of the covered colonnade in the Temple (EV, porch), Jhn.10:23 Act.3:11 5:12 † (AS)

712116.full: a plant used for stuffing or padding; and metaphorically " padding , " an expletive , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

s: The material elements of the universe
712117.full: στοιχεῖον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Wis.7:17 19:18, 4Ma.12:13 * ;] prop., one of a row (στοῖχος) or series, hence, __1. the shadow-line of a dial (Aristoph.). __2. an elementary sound or letter of the alphabet (Anth., Plut., π.). __3. the elements or rudiments of knowledge (Arist., al.) Heb.5:12; πτωχὰ σ., Gal.4:9; σ. τοῦ κόσμου, Gal.4:3, Col.2:8, 20 (but see infr.). __4. The material elements of the universe (Plat.; LXX, ll. with): 2Pe.3:10 3:12. __5. The heavenly bodies (Ding. Laert.). __6. The demons or tutelary spirits of nature (Enoch., Test., Sol., al.; for this sense in Ga, Col, ll. with, see ICC on Col.2:8; Enc. Bibl., see word " Elements ").† (AS)

s: in late writers, to walk by rule
712119.full: στοιχέω, -ῶ (στοῖχος, a row), [in LXX: Ecc.11:6 (כָּשֵׁר) * ;] to be in rows (of waves, plants, etc., as well as of men), to walk in line (esp. of marching in file to battle; Xen., Cyr., vi, 3, 34, al.). Metaphorical, in late writers, to walk by rule: Act.21:24; with dative, to walk by or in (as a rule of life), Rom.4:12 (cf. MM, xxiii), Gal.5:25 6:16, Php.3:16 (cf. συν-στοιχέω).† (AS)

712120.lxx: in LXX chiefly for בֶּגֶד, also for לְבוּשׁ, etc.
712120.full: στολή, -ῆς, ἡ (στέλλω), [in LXX chiefly for בֶּגֶד, also for לְבוּשׁ, etc. ;] __1 1, an equipment, an armament (Æsch.). __2. Equipment in clothes, apparel, esp. flowing raiment, a festal robe: (cf. Jon.3:6, Est.8:15, 1Ma.6:15): Mrk.12:38 16:5, Luk.15:22 20:46, Rev.6:11 7:9, 13-14 22:14.† (AS)

712121.full: 1. to put in trim , στολίσας νηὸς πτερά having trimmed the sails, (Hesiod) 2. to equip, dress :—;Pass., ἐστολισμένος δορί armed with spear, (Euripides) 3. metaphorically to deck, adorn , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

712125.full: στόμα, -τος, τό [in LXX chiefly for פֻּם ;] the mouth: of man, Mat.15:11, Jhn.19:29, Act.11:8, al.; of animals, Mat.17:27, 2Ti.4:17 (fig.), Heb.11:33, Jas.3:3, al.; figuratively, of inanimate things (ποταμοῦ, Hom.), ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ σ., Rev.12:16; σ. μαχαίρας (Heb. חֶרֶב ־פֶּה, Gen.34:26 al.), the edge of the sword, Luk.21:24, Heb.11:34; esp. of the mouth as the organ of speech: opposite to καρδία, Mat.12:34, Rom.10:8, 10; in various phrases (some cl., some resembling Hebrew; cf. Bl., § 40, 9): ἀνοίγειν τ. σ. (see: ἀνοίγω); σ. πρὸς σ. (פֶּה ־אֵל פֶּה Num.12:8; = cl., κατὰ σ., Hdt., al.), face to face, II Jn 12, 3Jn.14; διὰ τοῦ σ. (of the Holy Spirit), Luk.1:70, Act.1:16, al.; ἀπὸ (ἐκ) τοῦ σ. (cf. ἀπὸ σ. εἰπεῖν, Plat., al.), of speaking by word of mouth, Luk.22:71, Act.22:14; δόλος (ψεῦδος) ἐν τ. σ., 1Pe.2:22, Rev.14:5" (LXX) ; metaphorically, ἡ ῥομφαία τοῦ σ., Rev.2:16. By meton., for speech (Soph.): Mat.18:16 (LXX), Luk.19:22 21:15, 2Co.13:1 (AS)

712126.g: a scale which flies from hammered iron

s: to endeavour to make out, to guess
712129.full: 1. to aim or shoot at , with genitive, τοῦ σκοποῦ (Plato Philosophus), etc. 2. metaphorically to aim at, endeavour after , (Plato Philosophus); στ. φίλων κριτῶν to aim at having friends as judges, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to endeavour to make out, to guess at a thing, with genitive, (Isocrates Orator):—; absolute to make guesses, conjecture, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

712138.full: στρατεία (on the orthogr., see Deiss., BS, 181 f.), -ας, ἡ (οτρατεύω), [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;] an expedition, a campaign, warfare: metaphorically, 2Co.10:4 (-τιά, T), 1Ti.1:18.† (AS)

712139.full: στράτευμα, -τος, τό (στρατεύω), [in LXX: 1Ma.9:34, 2Ma.5:24 2Mac 8:21 2Mac 12:38 2Mac 13:13; pl., Jdth.11:8, 4Ma.5:1 * ;] __1. = στρατεία (Hdt., al.). __2. an army, a host: pl., Mat.22:7, Rev.9:16 19:14, 19; = soldiers, company of soldiers, Act.23:10, 27; pl., Luk.23:11.† (AS)

712140.lxx: in LXX for מההּ hith., יָצָא, צָבָא; metaphorically, 4Ma.9:23
712140.full: στρατεύω and depon., -ομαι, so always in NT (στρατός, an encamped army), [in LXX for מההּ hith., יָצָא, צָבָא; metaphorically, 4Ma.9:23 ;] used of the general, to make war, do battle, and (chiefly) of the soldiers serving under him, to serve as a soldier: Luk.3:14, 1Co.9:7, 2Ti.2:4. Metaphorical (cf. MM, ii, xxiii), of spiritual conflict, to war, make war: 2Co.10:3, 1Ti.1:18, Jas.4:1, 1Pe.2:11.† (AS)

712141.full: 1. to be general , (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;with genitive to be general of an army, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—; to lead as general , with dative, ἐστρατήγησε Λακεδαιμονίοισι (Herdotus Historicus); with accusative cognate, στρ. πόλεμον to conduct war, (Demosthenes Orator): with neuter adjective, to do a thing as general , τοῦτο (Xenophon Historicus); πάντα (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be conducted , (Plato Philosophus) 2. metaphorically, ποῦ σὺ στρατηγεῖς τοῦδ; how claim'st thou to command this man? (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

712143.full: 1. the office, dignity , or post of general, command , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; of naval command, (Xenophon Historicus) 2. the office of στρατηγός at Athens, a sort of war-minister , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;at Rome the Praetorship , (Plutarch) 3. a period of command, campaign , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. the qualities or skill of a general, generalship , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

s: A civic commander, a governor, magistrate
712144.lxx: in LXX chiefly for סָגָן (always in pl.), שַׂר
712144.full: στρατηγός, -οῦ, ὁ (στραός, ἄγω), [in LXX chiefly for סָגָן (always in pl.), שַׂר ;] __1. a military commander, a general (Hdt., al.). __2. A civic commander, a governor, magistrate (Hdt., Xen., al.): Act.16:20, 22 16:35-36, 38. __3. The commander of the Levitical guard of the Temple, ὁ σ. τ. ἱεροῦ (EV, captain of the Temple): Act.4:1 5:24, 26; pl., Luk.22:4, 52.† SYN.: ἄρχων (cf. EGT on Act.16:20; Ramsay, St. Paul, 217). (AS)

712145.full: στρατιά, -ᾶς, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;] __1. = στρατός, an army, a host: of angels (3Ki.22:19, al.), Luk.2:13; of the stars of heaven (Jer.8:2, 2Ch.33:3), Act.7:42. __2. As sometimes in cl. (poët.), = στρατεία: 2Co.10:4, T (WH, RV, στρατεία).† (AS)

712146.lxx: in LXX; 2Ki.23:8 B1, 2Ma.5:12 2Mac 14:39, III Mac  3:12; 3Ma.3:4 Mac3 *
712146.full: στρατιώτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX; 2Ki.23:8 B1, 2Ma.5:12 2Mac 14:39, III Mac 3:12; 3Ma.3:4 Mac3 * ;] a soldier: Mat.8:9, Mrk.15:16, Jhn.19:2, Act.10:7, al.; metaphorically, σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησ., 2Ti.2:3.† (AS)

712150.full: 1. to encamp, bivouac, take up a position , (Xenophon Historicus): 2. as Dep. στρατοπεδεύομαι, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; perfect ἐστρατοπεδεῦσθαι to be in camp , (Xenophon Historicus): of a fleet, to be stationed , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

712151.full: στρατό-πεδον, -ου, τό (στρατός + πέδον, a plain), [in LXX: Jer.34:1 (חַיִל), 2Ma.8:12, al. ;] __(a) a military camp; __(b) an army: Luk.21:20.† (AS)

712154.full: twisted, crooked , (Aristotle Philosopher); of the brows, knit, wrinkled , [variant datesAnthology Palantina: metaphorically, στρεβλοῖσι παλαίσμασι by cunning dodges in wrestling, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

712155.full: στρεβλόω, -ῶ (στρέφω), [in LXX: 2Ki.22:27 (פָּתַל hithp.), 3Ma.4:14, 4Ma.9:17 4Mac 12:4 4Mac 12:11 4Mac 15:14 * ;] to twist, torture. Metaphorical (cf. 2Ki, l.with), to twist or pervert language: 2Pe.3:16.† (AS)

712158.full: 1. flexible, pliant : στρεπτὸς χιτών a shirt of chain-armour , Lat. lorica annulata, (Iliad by Homer); στρεπταὶ λύγοι pliant withs, (Euripides): twined, wreathed , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. στρεπτός, οῦ, a collar of twisted or linked metal , Lat. torques, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 3. of pastry, a twist or roll , (Demosthenes Orator) 4. metaphorically to be bent or turned , στρεπτοὶ καὶ θεοὶ αὐτοί the gods themselves may be turned (by prayer), (Iliad by Homer); στρ. γλῶσσα a glib, pliant tongue, (Iliad by Homer) 5. bent, curved , of a pick-axe, (Euripides); of a bow, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

712160.lxx: in LXX chiefly for הָפַךְ, also for סָבַב, etc.
712160.full: στρέφω [in LXX chiefly for הָפַךְ, also for סָבַב, etc. ;] to turn: with accusative of thing(s) dative of person(s), Mat.5:39; = ἀποσ-, to bring back, Mat.27:3 (cf. Isa.38:8); reflexively (WM, § 38, 1), to turn oneself, Act.7:42; with accusative before εἰς, = μετασ-, to change, Rev.11:6. Pass., reflexive, to turn oneself: before εἰς, Jhn.20:14, Act.7:39 13:46; ptcp., στραφείς, with indic., Mat.7:6 9:22 16:23, Luk.7:9 9:55 14:25 22:61, Jhn.1:38 20:16; id. before πρός, Luk.7:44 10:22 (WH, R, om.), Luk.7:23 23:28; metaphorically, to change: absol., Mat.18:3, Jhn.12:40 (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στρέφω).† (AS)

712161.full: στρῆνος, -ους, τό (cf. Lat. strenuus), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:28 (שַׁאֲנָן)* ;] insolent luxury, wantonness: Rev.18:3 (a late word, first found in a Comic poet, B.C. 300, see Kennedy, Sources, 41, cf. στρηνιάω).† (AS)

712163.full: to twist, twirl or whirl about , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;metaphorically to make dizzy, distract , (Aeschulus Tragicus): —;Pass. to whirl about , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

712165.full: 1. round, spherical , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; λίθοι στρ. pebbles , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. circular , (Plato Philosophus) 3. round, compactly formed , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. of ships, στρ. ναῦς, στρ. πλοῖον, a merchant- ship, from its round shape , as opposite to the long narrow ship-of-war μακρὰ ναῦς); (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 5. metaphorically of phrases, well-rounded, compact, pithy, terse , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;adverb, στρογγυλώτατα as tersely as possible , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

712166.full: στρουθίον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר ;] dimin. of στρουθός a sparrow: Mat.10:29, 31, Luk.12:6-7.† (AS)

712167.full: 1. the sparrow , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. ὁ μέγας στρ. the large bird , i. e. the ostrich, Struthio , (Xenophon Historicus): also called στρουθὸς κατάγαιος (i. e. the bird that runs on the ground , does not fly), (Herdotus Historicus); also simply στρουθός, like στρουθοκάμηλος, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

712168.full: the socket in which the pivot of a door ὁ στρόφιγξ); moved, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

s: as they danced from right to left of the
the strain sung during this evolution, the strophe
712169.full: 1. a turning , e.g. of a horse, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν στροφαῖσιν ὀμμάτων with rolling of the eyes, (Euripides) 2. a twist , such as wrestlers make to elude their adversary, (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically a trick, dodge , (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. the turning of the Chorus as they danced from right to left of the ὀρχήστρα: the strain sung during this evolution, the strophe , to which the ἀντιστροφή answers. (ML)

s: pin on which a body turns
712170.full: 1. the pivot, axle or pin on which a body turns , (Euripides) 2. στρόφιγγες were pivots working in sockets , at top and bottom of a door, which served instead of hinges, (Plutarch) 3. metaphorically, στρ. γλώττης, of a well-hung tongue, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

s: the bedclothes, the coverings of a dinner-couch
712173.full: 1. anything spread or laid out for lying or sitting upon, a mattress, bed , Lat. stragulum, vestis stragula, (Theognis Elegiacus):—;in plural the bedclothes, the coverings of a dinner-couch , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 2. a horsecloth, horse-trappings , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

712174.full: a bed spread or prepared; generally, a bed, couch , (Pindar), etc.: a mattress, bedding , (Xenophon Historicus); στρ. ἄφθιτος, of the golden fleece, (Pindar) from στρώτης (ML)

712175.lxx: in LXX for יַצַע hoph., etc.
712175.full: στρωννύω or στρώννυμι (seeBl., § 23, 1; Veitch, see word), [in LXX for יַצַע hoph., etc. ;] to spread: ἱμάτια ἐν τ. ὁδῷ (εἰς τ. ὁδόν), Mat.21:8, Mrk.11:8; of making a bed, στρῶσον (sc. τ. κλίνην) σεαυτῷ, Act.9:34; of furnishing a room, ἐστρωμένον, spread with carpets or carpeted couches (cf. Eze.23:41), Mrk.14:15, Luk.22:12.† (AS)

s: to have a sombre, gloomy appearance
712177.full: στυγνάζω (στυγνός, sombre, gloomy, sullen, Isa.5:17, Wis.17:5, Dan LXX 2:12*), [in LXX: Eze.27:35 28:19 32:10 (שָׁמֵם)* ;] to have a sombre, gloomy appearance: of the human countenance (RV, his countenance fell), Mrk.10:22; of the sky (so στυγνότης, Polyb., iv, 21, 1), Mat.16:3 ([WH], R, mg., om.).† (AS)

712178.full: 1. hated, abhorred, hateful , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;with dative hateful or hostile to one, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. gloomy, sullen , Lat. tristis, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὁρᾶν στυγνός gloomy to behold, (Xenophon Historicus);—; στυγνὸς εἴκων yielding sullenly, with an ill grace , (Sophocles Tragicus); neuter as adverb, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

s: a pillar, regarded especially as a support
712179.lxx: in LXX chiefly for עַמּוּד, also for קֶרֶשׁ, etc.
712179.full: στύλος (T, στῦλος, as in cl.), -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for עַמּוּד, also for קֶרֶשׁ, etc. ;] a pillar, regarded especially as a support: σ. πυρός, Rev.10:1; σ. ἐν τ. ναῷ, figuratively, Rev.3:12, Metaphorical, Gal.2:9; τ. ἀληθείας, 1Ti.3:15.† (AS)

712180.full: made of the wood of the tree στύραξ, (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

712181.full: σύ, pron. of 2nd of person(s), thou, you, genitive, σοῦ, dative, σοί, accusative, σέ, pl., ὑμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς (enclitic in oblique cases sing., except after prep. (BL, §48, 3), though πρὸς σέ occurs in Mat.25:39). Nom. for emphasis or contrast: Jhn.1:30, 4:10, 5:33, 39, 44, Act.4:7, Eph.5:32; so also perhaps σὺ εἶπας, Mat.26:64, al. (M, Pr., 86); before voc., Mat.2:6, Luk.1:76, Jhn.17:5, al.; sometimes without emphasis (M, Pr., 85f.), as also in cl., but esp. as rendering of Heb. phrase, e.g. υἱός μου εἶ σύ (בְּנִי־אַתָּה, Psa.2:7), Act.13:33. The genitive (σοῦ, ὑμῶν) is sometimes placed bef. the noun: Luk.7:48, 12:30, al.; so also the enclitic σοῦ, Mat.9:6; on τί ἐμοὶ κ. σοί, see: ἐγώ. (AS)

712184.full: συγγένεια, -ας, ἡ (συγγενής), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּחָה ;] __1. kinship. __2. By meton., kinsfolk, kindred: Luk.1:61, Act.7:3, 14 † (AS)

712185.lxx: in LXX for דּוֹד, דּוֹדָה, מִשְׁפָּחָה
712185.full: σνγγενής, -ές (dative pl., -εῦσιν, Mrk.6:4, Luk.2:44, as though from -εύς, see Swete, Mk., l.with; Bl., § 8, 6; cf. 1Ma.10:89 A א2 *;) (σύν, γένος), [in LXX for דּוֹד, דּוֹדָה, מִשְׁפָּחָה ;] __1. congenital, natural, innate. __2. akin to; as subst., a kinsman: Mrk.6:4, Luk.1:58 2:44 14:12 21:16, Jhn.18:26, Act.10:24; of tribal kinship, Rom.9:3 16:7, 11 16:21.† SYN.: ἴδιος, οἰκεῖος (which see) (AS)

712188.full: συν-γνώμη (Rec. συγγ-), -ης, ἡ (συγγιγνώσκω, (a) to agree with; (b) to pardon), [in LXX: Sir prol.14 (B1N1 cm.) 313, 2Mac 14:20* ;] __1. confession. __2. fellow feeling; hence, concession, allowance: 1Co.7:6 (see ICC, in l). __3. pardon.† (AS)

s: that which is written, a writing, book: a history, narrative
a written contract, a covenant, bond
712192.full: 1. a writing or noting down , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. that which is written, a writing, book: a history, narrative , (Thucydides), etc. 3. a written contract, a covenant, bond , Lat. syngrapha, (Thucydides); συγγ. ναυτικαί a bond to secure money lent on bottomry, (Demosthenes Orator); ἀνδριάντα ἐκδεδωκὼς κατὰ συγγραφήν having contracted for its execution, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

712195.full: συν-κάθημαι (Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Psa.101:6 (יָשַׁב) * ;] to sit together or with: with dative, Act.26:30; before μετά, with genitive, Mrk.14:54.† (AS)

712196.lxx: in LXX for חָנָה, לָחַם ni., etc.
712196.full: περι-καθ-ίζω [in LXX for חָנָה, לָחַם ni., etc. ;] __1. to invest, besiege (Diod., 4Ki.6:24, 1Ma.11:61, al.). __2. to sit around: Luk.22:55, L, txt. † (AS)

712198.full: set on fire with or at once, burn up , Lat. comburere, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

712199.full: συν-καλέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, [in LXX for קָרָא ;] to call together: with accusative, Mrk.15:16, Luk.15:6, 9 (seel. -εῖται, see B1., § 55, 1), Act.5:21. Mid., to call together to oneself: Luk.9:1 (and seel. in Luk.15:6, 9 see supr.) Luk.23:13, Act.10:24 28:17.† (AS)
